source.chiefComplaint: Crushing chest pressure radiating to left arm and jaw for 90 minutes
source.historyOfPresentIllness: Sudden heavy pressure in the centre of the chest began while working in the garage 90 minutes before this consultation. It radiates to the lower jaw and left arm. Cold sweat and nausea accompanied the pain. Rest has not relieved it.

historyClues.questionText: Can you describe the pain? Is it sharp, tearing, or pressure-like?
historyClues.patientAnswer: It's not sharp at all. It's a heavy, dull crushing weight. Like my chest is squeezed in a vise.

historyClues.questionText: Did the pain start suddenly or build up gradually?
historyClues.patientAnswer: It hit me suddenly about an hour and a half ago. It hasn't let up even for a second.

historyClues.questionText: Do you have medical conditions like diabetes, high blood pressure, or cholesterol?
historyClues.patientAnswer: Yes, I have high blood pressure and type 2 diabetes. I'll admit I haven't been taking my blood pressure pills regularly lately.

historyClues.questionText: Do you smoke or use other substances?
historyClues.patientAnswer: I smoke about a pack a day for the past 30 years. No drugs though.

historyClues.questionText: Any family members with heart attacks at an early age?
historyClues.patientAnswer: My father had a fatal heart attack when he was only 52.

historyClues.questionText: Have you taken any erectile dysfunction medications like Viagra recently?

physicalExamFindings.findings: Moderately distressed, pale, diaphoretic, clutching his sternum with a closed fist (Levine sign positive).
Tachycardic, regular rhythm. Normal S1 and S2. Soft S4 gallop present at the apex. No murmurs or friction rubs heard.
Mild tachypnea. Clear to auscultation bilaterally. No wheezing, crackles, or rhonchi.
JVP is flat at 30 degrees. Radial and femoral pulses are equal and symmetrical bilaterally with brisk upstroke.
Soft, non-tender, non-distended. Normal bowel sounds. No pulsatile abdominal mass.

investigations.name: 12-Lead Electrocardiogram (ECG)
investigations.result: Sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm. Marked 3.5 mm ST-segment elevation in leads V1, V2, V3, and V4 with hyperacute T waves. Reciprocal ST depression in leads II, III, and aVF.

investigations.name: High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin I
investigations.result: hs-cTnI: 480 ng/L (Markedly elevated; Reference URL < 14 ng/L).

investigations.name: Portable Chest Radiograph
investigations.result: Normal cardiothoracic ratio. Mediastinal contours normal without widening. Clear lung parenchyma without pulmonary edema or pneumothorax.

investigations.name: Basic Metabolic Panel (BMP)
investigations.result: Na: 138 mEq/L, K: 4.1 mEq/L, Cl: 101 mEq/L, HCO3: 24 mEq/L, BUN: 18 mg/dL, Cr: 1.0 mg/dL, Glucose: 172 mg/dL.

investigations.name: Coagulation Panel (PT/INR, aPTT)
investigations.result: PT: 12.1 sec, INR: 1.0, aPTT: 28 sec (Within normal limits).

opening_line: Dobar dan, doktore. Već sat i po me jako pritišće u prsima i ne popušta ni kad mirujem.

source.chiefComplaint: Right lower quadrant abdominal pain for 14 hours with nausea and vomiting
source.historyOfPresentIllness: Dull pain began around the belly button 14 hours before this consultation. Over the last 6 hours it moved to the right lower abdomen and became sharp and constant. Walking hurts. Vomited twice after the pain started and has no appetite.

historyClues.questionText: When was your Last Menstrual Period (LMP)?
historyClues.patientAnswer: It was about 3 weeks ago, normal flow.

historyClues.questionText: Are you sexually active, and could you possibly be pregnant?
historyClues.patientAnswer: I am sexually active, but we use condoms. I really don't think I am pregnant.

historyClues.questionText: Did the nausea and vomiting start before or after the abdominal pain?
historyClues.patientAnswer: The pain started first around dinner time. The nausea came on later in the middle of the night.

historyClues.questionText: Any burning with urination, frequency, or vaginal discharge?
historyClues.patientAnswer: No burning and no unusual discharge.

physicalExamFindings.findings: Maximal exquisite tenderness at McBurney's point. Marked involuntary guarding in the RLQ.
Rovsing sign positive (palpation of LLQ causes pain in RLQ). Psoas sign positive (pain on passive right hip extension).
No cervical motion tenderness. Normal adnexa without palpable masses or fullness.

investigations.name: Urine & Serum Beta-hCG (Pregnancy Test)
investigations.result: Negative (< 2 mIU/mL). Confirms patient is not pregnant.

investigations.name: Complete Blood Count (CBC)
investigations.result: WBC 14,800/uL with 86% neutrophils and 8% band forms (marked left shift). Hemoglobin 13.2 g/dL.

investigations.name: Graded Compression Abdominal Ultrasound
investigations.result: Non-compressible, blind-ending tubular structure in RLQ measuring 8.2 mm in diameter with target sign and hyperemic wall vascularity on color Doppler. Mild pericecal fluid.

opening_line: Dobar dan, doktore. Od sinoć me boli stomak, a sad najviše dolje desno.
